summary: Sanders County, MT tower also called Clark Peak: built 1934 as a 20-foot L-4, staffed until 1969, destroyed 1970; no source describes the site now.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1970 per the Sanders County Ledger; firelookout.com says destroyed in the 1970s.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts page places the tower in the Kootenai National Forest; firelookout.com places it in the Lolo National Forest. The facts block uses the Kootenai value, which matches the current record. The story reports both.
The Ledger column dates the destruction to 1970; firelookout.com says only that it was destroyed in the 1970s. The event uses 1970 and the story gives both.

sources.title: Remember When: Lookouts in Sanders County

notes_for_editor: Two independent write-ups (firelookout.com and the 2021 Ledger column) agree on the 1934 build, the 20-foot L-4 design and staffing to 1969. The forest is disputed (Lolo vs Kootenai) and the story says so; check which one the brief should carry. The Ledger spells the town Thomson Falls; the quote is kept as printed. A search surfaced Cougar Peak Lookout and other Sanders County lookouts; none is this site and none was used. No source describes the site today, and no source gives access.
